text:
tara: Quick sync: we still don't have a clear contract for who owns probe-driven route hints and their lifecycle. Compiler? runtime adapters? both? Want to avoid more canary-day surprises.

josh: My read: compiler owns the canonical graph and long-lived invariants; runtime adapters own ephemeral signals derived from probes/telemetry. But we need a formal adapter contract so runtimes won't corrupt compiler assumptions.

rafa: Suggest a 3-part contract: 1) Identity guarantees (shape_id + shape_sig in artifacts). 2) Namespaced probe keys (namespace + runtime_id + shape_id). 3) Advisory proof (compact fingerprint + confidence).

megan: Example of the identity piece: artifact header contains {shape_id:int, shape_sig:hex, compat_flags:[str], migration_hint?:map}. Runtimes must check shape_id and compat_flags before applying any advisory.

tara: We should avoid node-id reuse across non-consecutive shape_ids. Compiler CI should warn if a node id reappears with a gap. That caused the cache stomp last incident.

josh: For namespacing: runtime-written keys are keyed by (shape_id, namespace, runtime_id). On artifact swap, runtime cleans keys where shape_id < current-1. If migration_hint exists, runtime can translate keys per the map until migration_ttl expires.

rafa: Advisory proof format proposal: proof = xxh64(shape_sig || node_key || decision_delta || epoch). Accompany with confidence float and a tiny namespace tag. Make epoch monotonic per runtime to prevent simple replay.

megan: Acceptance rules at decision time: 1) proof valid -> maps to a node in the current artifact index OR translated via migration_map. 2) confidence >= route-specific threshold (default 0.7). 3) advisory doesn't violate compiler-specified guard rails (e.g., must not route outside allowed regions or tiers).

tara: If any check fails runtime must fallback to compiled default and emit a metric. Also record a short debug log with proof_fingerprint for postmortem.

josh: One open tradeoff: proof size and verification cost. I think keep proof 8 bytes and do a constant-time artifact index lookup. Add an async deep-validate that computes a semantic check later and raises an alert if mismatch.

rafa: Migration maps are useful but can be misused. Add CI lint: migration_map length > 128 -> require arch review and a manual rollout flag. Large remaps indicate non-additive changes and need coordination.

megan: Also enforce a conservative runtime sweep rule during canary: runtimes accept advisories only when artifact.shape_id in {current, current-1}. This keeps overlap windows simple.

tara: We should also define idempotency for probes: include probe_uuid, and runtime should not double-charge tokens or apply the same advisory twice if probe_uuid seen recently. Keep an LRU of recent probe_uuids with small ttl.

josh: Ops integration: policy-service should have a tiny verifier endpoint that can be called synchronously to validate proofs using the artifact index. If verifier returns unknown proof, runtime rejects immediately; if verifier accepts, it returns a compact node_id the runtime can use. Heavy diffs run async.

rafa: Security note: proofs must never encode secrets or tenant data. They are purely deterministic fingerprints. Also rate-limit probe acceptance: per-tenant probe budgets to avoid noisy tenants causing oscillation (separate RFC).

megan: Rollout checklist idea: compiler must emit shape_id increment and optional migration_map; CI ensures no reuse of node ids across non-consecutive shape_ids; runtimes behind feature flag validate proofs; small canary window with metrics observed; then enable globally.

tara: Can we sketch a minimal artifact header example for docs? Something like: 
```json
{"shape_id":243,"shape_sig":"b7e1f2","compat_flags":["accept_probe_v1","kv_namespacing_v1"],"migration_hint":{"old/node/7":"new/node/12"},"builder":"policy-compiler-3"}
```

josh: Good. Also sketch a probe envelope example the runtime emits: 
```json
{"namespace":"probe-west-01","runtime_id":"rt-77","shape_id":243,"proof":"0x9f1b2c3d4a","confidence":0.78,"probe_uuid":"p-1234","epoch":162345}
```

rafa: Add metrics: policy.advisory.accept, policy.advisory.reject.reason, policy.advisory.verify_latency, policy.advisory.migration_applied. These will help detect mismatches quickly.

megan: Tests: add unit tests for proof verification, small fuzz tests for collisions, and integration tests where compiler emits a migration_map and runtimes exercise translation.

tara: Action items: megan draft the adapter-contract RFC with examples and tests; josh add CI lints for node-id reuse and migration_map size; rafa prototype small verifier endpoint and artifact index format; I'll schedule an arch-checkin next Tuesday for signoff.

ci-bot: build:policy-compiler-3 -> canary 5% :white_check_mark: <https://ci/redwood/11177>

tara: Thanks team. Keep the RFC focused and include two short policy scenarios (latency-first accepted advisory, cost-first low-confidence rejected advisory) so reviewers can exercise both flows.
